messages:
maria: seeing a weird tail-latency spike in ap-northeast yesterday evening — not classic oom or preempt. p95 fine, p99+ jumps and stays elevated for ~20m. digging now.

ev an: can you paste the heatmap or a logs snippet? region only or global?

maria: looks az-localized. only nodes in ap-northeast-2a. other AZs normal. stack traces point at long waits inside batching queue, not GPU throttles.

ev an: hmm batch queue growth usually means a single tenant doing bursty long-context inferences. any tenant id in the traces?

maria: yes — recovered job ids show heavy seq-length 8k requests from a single customer during the window. not sure why it stuck to 2a.

sam: could be our routing preference — we favor lower-cost AZ for that pool, so sticky flows sometimes pile up. we have a known imbalance in capacity across AZs (we reduced gpus in 2b last month).

jia: is this on shared pools or dedicated?

maria: shared. the request was grad-school customer on free-tier. kept getting routed to available slots in 2a.

sam: two angles: 1) make routing AZ-aware with soft spread + active balancing 2) limit per-tenant inflight across AZs so a burst can't consume all slots in one AZ.

ev an: agree. Also consider short-term mitigation: weigh capacity by headroom and apply per-az fairshare. That would avoid pileups when one AZ is low.

maria: testable change: add per-tenant per-az soft concurrency cap (default 6) and fall back to other az if cap hit. We should experiment in canary.

sam: notes: cost impact if we start cross-az routing more often — egress charges and higher latencies. need to quantify.

jia: we should also check cache-priming effects. long contexts can balloon kv cache memory and cause slower evictions that slow everyone. any mem pressure logs?

maria: attaching small excerpt: ```
2026-06-12T20:03:12Z INFO batching_queue length=42 tenant=acme-corp seq_len=8192 node=ap-northeast-2a
2026-06-12T20:03:14Z WARN kv_cache_evict slow_eviction_ms=230 tenant=acme-corp node=ap-northeast-2a
2026-06-12T20:03:30Z INFO gpu_util 98% node=ap-northeast-2a
```

ev an: that slow_eviction is an indicator — long contexts cause large KV sets and eviction loops. even if GPU isn't starved, CPU/PCIe and scheduling degrade.

sam: plan proposal: (A) add per-tenant per-az soft concurrency cap + a greedy reroute to next-best-az when cap hit; (B) throttle very-long-context requests via a lightweight admission controller that can ask client to retry with smaller chunking; (C) add a short-term autoscale bump for 2a if policy allows.

jia: also add a telemetry tag for "kv_cache_bytes" per tenant so we can track these events and set alerts (p99 kv_cache_bytes > X).

maria: implemented a canary PR for the per-az cap but need someone from infra-scheduling to approve. ping @sam for review?

sam: on it. quick thought on fallback: prefer same-region AZs before cross-region to avoid egress. fallback order: 2a -> 2b -> 2c then cross-region.

ev an: we must ensure fairshare accounting still counts re-routed requests against tenant global concurrency, else tenants will bypass limits by scattering.

jia: agree. hits should be global-inflight tracked, with per-az caps being a local gate.

maria: created the PR and linked a dashboard with the canary metrics. PR link: https://git.company/repo/pull/1123 (commented steps to roll out to 2a canary).

sam: rolling to canary tonight. metrics to watch: p99 latency, batching_queue length, kv_cache_evict latency, per-az tenant inflight.

infra-bot: deploy triggered for "per-az-soft-cap" -> env=ap-northeast canary. job=deploy-789 status=started

maria: thanks. follow-up: if canary looks good, we should prepare a customer-communication playbook for tenants that hit new throttles (esp free-tier research users). short note + recommended chunking guide.

ev an: +1. also evaluate adding a cost estimate: per-az autoscale to avoid pileups may cost X/month. sam can you rough that out?

sam: will run numbers — initial estimate: adding 8 gpus to 2a reserved pool ~ $12k/mo, vs small lat penalty for reroute that costs < $1k/mo in egress. will post a breakdown.

maria: ok will monitor canary and post results in ~2h. thanks all :thumbsup:
